• Scientific name: Loricaria cataphracta Linnaeus, 1758
  • Common names: L062, Cataphract Whiptail
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2020)
Family: Loricariidae. Size: 20 cm. Temperature: 24–28°C. pH: 6.5–7.0. L-number: L062. IUCN: Least Concern (IUCN 2023).
Sensitive to poor water quality especially when first imported and should be acclimatised slowly for the home aquarium.

South America: Amazon River basin and coastal rivers of the Guianas, including the Lower Amazon (Nhamundá), Guyana, and Suriname coastal rivers (Marowijne). Type locality: mouth of the Marowijne River, near Galibi, Suriname.
South America: Amazon River basin, and coastal rivers of the Guianas, Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname. Type locality: In America meridionali.
Carnivore, feed with tablets, pellets, insect larvae, zooplankton and shrimps. A varied diet is important to this species and genus.

Loricaria species can be differentiated from the similar Rineloricaria species by their feathered sucker-mouths, which the males use for carrying their eggs around after spawning; they are maternal mouthbrooders.
When young, Loricaria spp. can be differentiated from the similar Rineloricaria spp. by their more feathered sucker-mouths. In adults this difference is considerably more evident.

Not the easiest of genera to identify to species; the key for the Loricaria genus is teeth of the upper jaw about twice as long as those of the lower jaw. Abdomen ventrally completely covered by scutes.

Etymology: The specific name cataphracta is Latin for wearing coats of mail (armour), referring to bony plates on back and sides.
